mainTopic: Is the ruling of רבי יוחנן בן נורי (multiple liabilities for one act with his mother-in-law) the same as the view of סומכוס (eighty lashes in a case of אותו ואת בנו)? רבא and רב נחמן בר יצחק each show why the two views need not depend on each other.
overview: The amud opens by finishing a ברייתא in which סומכוס gives eighty lashes for slaughtering the middle animal of three generations on one day. רבא and רב נחמן בר יצחק each show why the view of רבי יוחנן בן נורי about a mother-in-law does not have to match סומכוס. One points to separate names and the other to separate bodies. Then a new משנה tells how רבי עקיבא asked רבן גמליאל and רבי יהושע about a man who sins with his sister, his father's sister and his mother's sister. The גמרא explains that the case is one woman who carries all three labels. A קל וחומר from five wives who are נדות fails, so the rule that each label counts is learned from the פסוק "ערות אחותו גלה". רב אדא בר אהבה shows how such a family can exist. A ברייתא then brings the dispute between רבי אליעזר and the חכמים about repeated acts with one woman. רבה and רב יוסף argue over whether רבי אליעזר's reason also applies to reaping twice on שבת, and רבה survives אביי's challenge. Finally a new משנה begins with רבי עקיבא's question about a limb dangling from an animal, and the answer continues on the next amud.

steps.title: The case of three generations of animals slaughtered on one day
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא finishes quoting a ברייתא. If someone slaughters a grandmother animal and its granddaughter, and then the middle animal, the תנא קמא says he gets forty lashes. סומכוס in the name of רבי מאיר says he gets eighty.
steps.simpleTranslation: If a person slaughtered an animal and its granddaughter, and afterward slaughtered the middle animal (the daughter), he receives the forty lashes. סומכוס says in the name of רבי מאיר: he receives eighty lashes.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is bringing a ברייתא to show that סומכוס holds one act can make a person liable twice under the same prohibition. It wants to show that רבי יוחנן בן נורי holds the same idea.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When the middle animal is slaughtered, it is the 'child' of the grandmother and the 'mother' of the granddaughter. Both of those animals were already slaughtered that day, so one act breaks אותו ואת בנו twice. The תנא קמא gives only one set of forty lashes, but סומכוס gives two sets (eighty).

keyTerms.meaning: The prohibition against slaughtering a mother animal and its offspring on the same day
Receives (a punishment), here meaning he is given lashes
The forty lashes, the standard punishment for breaking a לא תעשה
Eighty, meaning two full sets of lashes

steps.confusionAlert: The order of slaughtering matters. The middle animal is slaughtered last, so it is connected to both of the animals already slaughtered that day. That is why one act could count twice.

phrases.english: If he slaughtered it and its daughter's daughter,
and afterward slaughtered its daughter –
he receives the forty lashes.
Sumakhos says in the name of Rabbi Meir:
He receives eighty.

steps.triggerLanguage: שְׁחָטָהּ וְאֶת בַּת בִּתָּהּ, וְאַחַר כָּךְ שָׁחַט אֶת בִּתָּהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the ברייתא quoted to compare רבי יוחנן בן נורי with סומכוס (the comparison began before this section).
steps.raayaObject: That רבי יוחנן בן נורי holds like סומכוס: one act that breaks one פסוק's prohibition twice brings double liability.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא in which סומכוס gives eighty lashes for slaughtering the middle animal of three generations.

steps.title: רבא: רבי יוחנן בן נורי may rely on separate names
steps.stepSummary: רבא suggests the comparison may be wrong. רבי יוחנן בן נורי may give multiple liabilities only because the Torah calls the woman by different names: mother-in-law, mother-in-law's mother, and father-in-law's mother.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: Perhaps that is not so. רבי יוחנן בן נורי only said his ruling here because of the different names: she is called 'his mother-in-law,' she is called 'his mother-in-law's mother,' and she is called 'his father-in-law's mother.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבא rejects the claim that רבי יוחנן בן נורי must agree with סומכוס. He gives a special reason for רבי יוחנן בן נורי's ruling that may not apply to animals.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא says רבי יוחנן בן נורי's reason may not be the general idea that one act can count twice. His reason may be that each relative has her own separate name in the Torah, which makes each one a separate prohibition. If so, his ruling depends on that detail and not on the view of סומכוס.

keyTerms.meaning: Perhaps it is not so, an opening for rejecting a comparison
He only said his ruling up to this point, meaning his ruling may be limited to this case
Separate names, meaning different labels the Torah uses for each prohibition
His mother-in-law
His father-in-law's mother

phrases.english: Rava said: Perhaps it is not so,

phrases.aramaic: עַד כָּאן לָא קָאָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן בֶּן נוּרִי הָכָא
phrases.english: Rabbi Yoḥanan ben Nuri said his ruling here
phrases.notes: 'Here' means the case of a man with his mother-in-law, where רבי יוחנן בן נורי gave more than one liability.

phrases.english: only because of differentiated names,
as she is called his mother-in-law,
and she is called his mother-in-law's mother,
and she is called his father-in-law's mother.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רָבָא: דִּלְמָא לָא הִיא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the attempt to use the ברייתא of סומכוס to explain רבי יוחנן בן נורי.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects only the link between the two views. It does not reject either ruling itself.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The comparison misses a key difference: the relatives each have a separate name, and this may be the true reason for רבי יוחנן בן נורי's ruling.

steps.title: With animals there are no separate names
steps.stepSummary: רבא finishes his point. With אותו ואת בנו, every case is called by the same single name, so רבי יוחנן בן נורי might not give double lashes there.
steps.simpleTranslation: But regarding אותו ואת בנו, where all the cases are called 'it and its offspring,' there are no separate names. So there, he would not say a person is liable twice.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא completes his rejection by spelling out the contrast. Animals have no separate names, so the reason he gave for רבי יוחנן בן נורי does not apply to them.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With animals, whether the mother or the young one is slaughtered first, the Torah uses the same label: 'it and its offspring.' Without separate names, רבי יוחנן בן נורי could agree with the תנא קמא that the person gets only forty lashes. So רבי יוחנן בן נורי does not have to hold like סומכוס.

keyTerms.meaning: Regarding, with respect to
They are called (by a name)

steps.whyThisMatters: This shows a key idea: double liability may depend on how the Torah names a prohibition, not only on how many violations the act contains.

phrases.english: But regarding a mother and its offspring,
where all of them are called 'it and its offspring,'
as there are no differentiated names – no.
phrases.notes: The word 'no' means רבי יוחנן בן נורי would not give double liability in this case.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲבָל גַּבֵּי אוֹתוֹ וְאֶת בְּנוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes רבא's rejection by applying his distinction to the case of the animals.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Shows that רבי יוחנן בן נורי could disagree with סומכוס.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: אותו ואת בנו does not have the separate names that drive רבי יוחנן בן נורי's ruling.

steps.title: רב נחמן בר יצחק: סומכוס may rely on separate bodies
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן בר יצחק rejects the comparison from the other side. סומכוס may give double lashes only in the case of animals, because there are separate bodies (different animals).
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן בר יצחק said: Perhaps סומכוס only said his ruling regarding אותו ואת בנו, because there are separate bodies.
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן בר יצחק also rejects the link between the two views. He limits the ruling of סומכוס instead of limiting רבי יוחנן בן נורי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the animal case, the one act is connected to two other animals, the mother and the granddaughter. That may be why סומכוס counts it twice. In the mother-in-law case there is only one woman, so סומכוס might not give multiple liabilities there.

keyTerms.meaning: Separate bodies, meaning different physical animals are involved

steps.whatToRemember: There are two ways to reject the comparison. רבא: רבי יוחנן בן נורי may depend on separate names, which animals lack. רב נחמן בר יצחק: סומכוס may depend on separate bodies, which one woman lacks. Either way, neither view has to depend on the other.

phrases.english: Rav Naḥman bar Yitzḥak said:

phrases.aramaic: דִּלְמָא עַד כָּאן לָא קָאָמַר סוֹמְכוֹס
phrases.english: Perhaps Sumakhos said his ruling
only regarding a mother and its offspring,
as there are differentiated bodies.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב נַחְמָן בַּר יִצְחָק: דִּלְמָא עַד כָּאן לָא קָאָמַר סוֹמְכוֹס
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a second, opposite rejection of the comparison. רבא limited רבי יוחנן בן נורי, while this step limits סומכוס.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the link between the two views by limiting the ruling of סומכוס to cases with separate bodies.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The mother-in-law case involves one body, unlike the three separate animals in the case of סומכוס.

steps.title: With one woman, סומכוס might count only one sin
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן בר יצחק finishes his rejection. With a mother-in-law there are no separate bodies, so סומכוס may agree with רבי אבהו in the name of רבי יוחנן that the פסוק makes all these relatives one זמה.
steps.simpleTranslation: But here, where there are not separate bodies, say that he holds like what רבי אבהו said in the name of רבי יוחנן. רבי אבהו said that רבי יוחנן said: "They are near kinswomen; it is lewdness." The פסוק made them all one single lewdness.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes רב נחמן בר יצחק's rejection from Step 4. In the mother-in-law case it is only one woman, so סומכוס might give just one liability.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In Step 4 we learned that סומכוס gives double lashes when there are separate animals. Here there is only one woman, so that reason is missing. Also, the פסוק ends with "זמה היא" (one lewdness), which can teach that all these relatives count as one sin. So neither side of the comparison holds up.

keyTerms.meaning: Close blood relatives (in the פסוק: "they are near kinswomen")
Lewdness, a word the תורה uses for certain forbidden relations
The פסוק made them (count as)

steps.whatToRemember: Both attempts to compare the cases were rejected. רבא pushed back from the side of רבי יוחנן בן נורי (different names), and רב נחמן בר יצחק pushed back from the side of סומכוס (separate bodies). With one woman, the פסוק may make it all one זמה.

phrases.english: But here, where there are not separate bodies,
phrases.notes: "Here" is the mother-in-law case. It is all one woman, unlike the separate animals.

phrases.english: say that like Rabbi Abbahu
phrases.notes: He means that סומכוס himself might hold this way.

phrases.english: said in the name of Rabbi Yochanan, he holds,

phrases.aramaic: דְּאָמַר רַבִּי אֲבָהוּ אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן:
phrases.english: as Rabbi Abbahu said that Rabbi Yochanan said:
"They are near kinswomen; it is lewdness"
phrases.notes: ויקרא 18:17

phrases.english: the verse made them all one single lewdness.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲבָל הָכָא, דְּאֵין גּוּפִין מוּחְלָקִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes רב נחמן בר יצחק's rejection begun in Step 4.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the idea that סומכוס's double lashes for animals prove he would give multiple liabilities in the mother-in-law case.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The animal case has separate bodies. The mother-in-law case is one woman, and the פסוק "זמה היא" may join all those relatives into one sin.

steps.title: רבי עקיבא asks about sister, father's sister and mother's sister
steps.stepSummary: A new משנה. רבי עקיבא tells how he asked רבן גמליאל and רבי יהושע in the meat market of Emmaus about a man who sinned with three different relatives: does he owe one חטאת or one for each?
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: רבי עקיבא said: I asked רבן גמליאל and רבי יהושע in the meat market of Emmaus, where they went to buy an animal for the feast of רבן גמליאל's son. One who has relations with his sister, his father's sister and his mother's sister, what is the law? Is he liable once for all of them, or liable for each and every one?
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה opens with a question. רבי עקיבא asked his teachers whether three different forbidden relatives bring one liability or three.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The case involves three women, each forbidden by its own prohibition. The question is whether he brings one חטאת for everything or a separate one for each woman. The story setting (buying meat for a wedding feast) just tells us where the question was asked.

keyTerms.meaning: Our משנה
Meat market
Feast (here, a wedding feast)
Liable once for all of them
For each and every one

phrases.english: MISHNA
Rabbi Akiva said:

phrases.aramaic: שָׁאַלְתִּי אֶת רַבָּן גַּמְלִיאֵל וְאֶת רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ
phrases.english: I asked Rabban Gamliel and Rabbi Yehoshua
in the meat market of Emmaus,
where they went to buy an animal
for the feast of Rabban Gamliel's son,
one who has relations with his sister

phrases.aramaic: וְעַל אֲחוֹת אָבִיו וְעַל אֲחוֹת אִמּוֹ, מַהוּ?
phrases.english: and his father's sister and his mother's sister, what is the law?
Is he liable once for all of them,
phrases.notes: "Liable" here means owing a חטאת, a sin offering.

phrases.aramaic: אוֹ חַיָּיב עַל כָּל אַחַת וְאֶחָת?
phrases.english: or liable for each and every one?

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא: שָׁאַלְתִּי אֶת רַבָּן גַּמְלִיאֵל וְאֶת רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new משנה begins, moving on from the previous ברייתא discussion.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי עקיבא asks whether sinning with his sister, his father's sister and his mother's sister brings one liability or a separate one for each.

steps.title: The teachers answer with five wives who are נדות
steps.stepSummary: רבן גמליאל and רבי יהושע say they did not hear this case. They did hear that a man who sins with his five wives who are נדות in one lapse owes for each one, and they see a קל וחומר from there.
steps.simpleTranslation: They said to him: We have not heard. But we have heard: one who has relations with his five wives while they are נדות, in one lapse of awareness, is liable for each and every one. And we see that the matter is a קל וחומר.
steps.whatsHappening: The teachers answer רבי עקיבא. They had no direct tradition, but they bring a related case they did hear and build a קל וחומר from it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Five wives who are נדות are all forbidden by one single prohibition (נדה), yet he owes a separate חטאת for each woman. So with three women forbidden by three different prohibitions, he should surely owe for each one. That is the קל וחומר.

keyTerms.meaning: A woman in her menstrual period, forbidden by one single prohibition
One lapse of awareness: he forgot the whole time and never realized in between
A logical argument from a lighter case to a stronger one

phrases.english: They said to him: We have not heard,
but we have heard:
one who has relations with his five wives who are niddah
in one lapse of awareness,
phrases.notes: Some versions have the word in round brackets; the corrected wording is in square brackets. Both mean "one."

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁהוּא חַיָּיב עַל כׇּל אַחַת וְאֶחָת,
phrases.english: that he is liable for each and every one,
and we see
phrases.notes: Some versions say "I see"; the corrected wording in square brackets says "we see," since both teachers are speaking.

phrases.english: that the matters are a kal vachomer.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמְרוּ לוֹ: לֹא שָׁמַעְנוּ, אֲבָל שָׁמַעְנוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רבי עקיבא's question from Step 6.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether three different forbidden relatives bring one liability or three.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: No direct tradition. But five wives who are נדות, all under one prohibition, bring a liability for each, so by קל וחומר three different prohibitions surely do.

steps.title: Why was רבי עקיבא unsure at all?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what case רבי עקיבא meant. If it is exactly as written, the answer is obvious: there are separate names and separate bodies.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: What is the case? If you say it is just as the משנה teaches, what was his question? Look, the names are separate, and the bodies are separate!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the משנה's question. As written, the case seems too obvious to ask about.
steps.deeperAnalysis: We saw earlier that separate names (different prohibitions) and separate bodies (different people) are each reasons to count many liabilities. Here the case has both: three women and three prohibitions. So the גמרא wonders why רבי עקיבא had any doubt, and this sets up an explanation of what case he really meant.

keyTerms.meaning: The talmudic discussion of the משנה
What is the case? What are the exact circumstances?
If you say (the גמרא offers a reading it will reject)
Separate names, meaning different prohibitions

steps.confusionAlert: The גמרא is not disagreeing with the answer of three liabilities. It is asking why the question was even asked, because the case as written seems obvious.

phrases.english: GEMARA
What is the case?
If you say it is as it teaches,
what is his question?
Look, the names are separate,
look, the bodies are separate!

steps.triggerLanguage: הֵיכִי דָמֵי? אִילֵּימָא כִּדְקָתָנֵי, מַאי תִּיבְּעֵי לֵיהּ?
steps.relationToPreviousStep: The גמרא begins analyzing the משנה, questioning the case behind רבי עקיבא's question.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי עקיבא's question in the משנה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Three women under three different prohibitions have both separate names and separate bodies, so separate liabilities seem obvious and there is nothing to ask.

steps.title: The real case: one woman with several forbidden labels
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers its own question from step 8. The משנה must be talking about a single woman who is both his father's sister and his mother's sister. So the doubt is whether separate names count, or whether one body makes it one חטאת.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, this is what the משנה is teaching: a man sins with his father's sister who is also his mother's sister. Does he owe one חטאת for all of them, or one for each? What is the law? Do we say that the names are separate? Or perhaps the bodies are not separate?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא fixes the problem from step 8 by changing the case. Now it is one woman who falls under several forbidden labels.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 8 the case was too easy, because three different women means separate names and separate bodies. Now there is only one woman, so the two signs point in opposite directions. Separate names suggest many חטאות, while one body suggests only one. That makes it a real question.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather, this is what it teaches. The גמרא is rereading the source.
His father's sister (aunt on the father's side)
His mother's sister (aunt on the mother's side)
Do we say... or perhaps. This sets out the two sides of a doubt.

steps.confusionAlert: Don't picture three women here. The whole point is that it is ONE woman with several labels. That is why there is any question at all.

phrases.english: Rather, this is what it teaches:
One who has relations with his father's sister
who is also his mother's sister,
is he liable one for all of them,

phrases.aramaic: אוֹ חַיָּיב עַל כׇּל אַחַת וְאֶחָת,
phrases.english: or is he liable for each and every one,
what is the law?
Do we say: here the names are separate,

phrases.aramaic: אוֹ דִלְמָא הֲרֵי אֵין גּוּפִין מוּחְלָקִין?
phrases.english: or perhaps: here the bodies are not separate?

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא הָכִי קָתָנֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 8 by redefining the case in the משנה
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי עקיבא asked about three different women, which would make the question obvious
steps.terutzMaskana: He asked about one woman with several forbidden labels: separate names but one body

steps.title: They had not heard this case, but knew about five wives who are נדות
steps.stepSummary: Read in its new light, the answer of רבן גמליאל and רבי יהושע says this: they had no tradition about one woman with many labels. They did know that a man who sins with his five wives who are נדות in one lapse brings a separate חטאת for each, even though it is only one name.
steps.simpleTranslation: They said to him: We did not hear about this. But we heard about one who has relations with his five wives who are נדות at one time, which is one name. He is liable for each and every one because of נדה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא repeats the answer from the משנה. It is setting up the קל וחומר that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here the five wives case is stressed as "one name" (שם אחד): every wife is forbidden only as a נדה. Even so, he brings a חטאת for each one. This will be the starting point of the קל וחומר.

keyTerms.meaning: We did not hear: we have no tradition from our teachers about this
At one time, meaning during one lapse of awareness
One name, meaning one category of prohibition
Because of the prohibition of a menstruating woman

phrases.english: They said to him: We did not hear,
but we did hear:
one who has relations with his five wives who are נדות
at one time, which is one name,
phrases.notes: "At one time" means he did it all while he was unaware the whole time, without stopping to realize it in between.

phrases.english: that he is liable for each and every one
because of נדה,

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמְרוּ לוֹ: לֹא שָׁמַעְנוּ, אֲבָל שָׁמַעְנוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rereads the answer from step 7 in light of the new case of step 9
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: There is no direct tradition. But five wives who are נדות, which is one name, still means a חטאת for each one.

steps.title: The קל וחומר: if one name counts five times, three names surely count
steps.stepSummary: The sages argue from easier to harder. Five wives who are נדות are one name, and he still brings a חטאת for each. So one woman who is his sister, his father's sister and his mother's sister, which are three names, should surely bring a חטאת for each label.
steps.simpleTranslation: We saw that the matter is a קל וחומר. If one who has relations with his five wives who are נדות at one time, which is one name, is liable for each one, then his sister who is his father's sister who is his mother's sister, which are three names, is it not logical that he should be liable for each one?
steps.whatsHappening: The sages use the five wives case to answer רבי עקיבא's question with a קל וחומר. They conclude that he brings a חטאת for each label.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The argument assumes that separate names are the thing that creates more חטאות. If one name could still bring five חטאות, three different names should certainly bring three. The weak point is that it ignores the difference in bodies.

keyTerms.meaning: And we saw: it seems to us by reasoning
"If even...", the opening word of a קל וחומר
Three names: three separate labels of prohibition
Is it not logical? This is the closing line of a קל וחומר.

phrases.english: And we saw that the matter is a קל וחומר:

phrases.aramaic: וּמָה הַבָּא עַל חָמֵשׁ נָשָׁיו נִדּוֹת
phrases.english: If one who has relations with his five wives who are נדות
at one time, which is one name
is liable for each and every one,
then his sister who is his father's sister
who is his mother's sister,
which are three names
is it not logical that he should be liable
for each and every one?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרָאִינוּ שֶׁהַדְּבָרִים קַל וָחוֹמֶר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds a קל וחומר from the five wives case of step 10 to answer the question of step 9
steps.raayaObject: One woman with three forbidden labels means a חטאת for each label
steps.raayaSupportSource: A קל וחומר from five wives who are נדות (one name, yet a חטאת for each one)

steps.title: The קל וחומר falls: the five wives are separate bodies
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא refutes the קל וחומר. The five wives bring separate חטאות because they are five different people. That is missing with one woman who has three labels.
steps.simpleTranslation: There is a way to refute this: what about five נדות? They are separate bodies!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא points out a weakness in the קל וחומר. The case it was built on has a strength of its own that the new case lacks.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The five wives are only one name, but they are five bodies, and maybe that is what gives five חטאות. The sister with three labels has three names but only one body. So the starting case is not "weaker" in every way, and the קל וחומר does not work.

keyTerms.meaning: There is a way to refute this. It introduces a challenge to a קל וחומר.
"What about X? For X has...": the pattern for showing that the starting case has its own strength
A refutation of a קל וחומר

steps.whatToRemember: Two things can make a man owe more than one חטאת: separate names (שמות מוחלקין) and separate bodies (גופין מוחלקין). The five wives have separate bodies. The sister with three labels has only separate names. So one case cannot be learned from the other.
steps.confusionAlert: The פירכא does not say that separate names never matter. It only says that the five wives case cannot prove they do, because something else (separate bodies) may be the reason there.

phrases.english: There is a way to refute this:
what about five נדות?
For they are separate bodies!

steps.triggerLanguage: אִיכָּא לְמִיפְרַךְ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Refutes the קל וחומר of step 11
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The proof from five wives who are נדות to one woman with three labels
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The starting case has separate bodies, which the case being learned lacks, so it is not weaker in every way

steps.title: The real source: the extra words in the פסוק
steps.stepSummary: The קל וחומר failed, so the גמרא brings a פסוק instead. 'עֶרְוַת אֲחוֹתוֹ גִלָּה' teaches that he is liable separately for a sister who is also his father's sister and his mother's sister.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, the פסוק says 'he has uncovered his sister's nakedness'. This makes him liable for his sister who is his father's sister and who is his mother's sister.
steps.whatsHappening: Logic alone could not prove that one woman with three labels means three חטאות. So the גמרא brings a פסוק that teaches it directly.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 12 the five-wives argument fell apart, because five wives are five different people. Now the source is the extra words at the end of the פסוק, which mention 'his sister' again. The extra words teach that each label counts on its own, even though it is one person.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather; drops the old approach and brings a new one
A forbidden relationship
His father's sister / his mother's sister

steps.whatToRemember: One woman with several forbidden labels does mean a separate חטאת for each label. This is learned from a פסוק, not from a קל וחומר.
steps.whyThisMatters: This settles the question רבי עקיבא raised. Separate names count even when there is only one body.

phrases.english: Rather, the verse says:
"He has uncovered his sister's nakedness"
phrases.notes: ויקרא 20:17. The same פסוק already mentioned 'his sister' earlier, so these words are extra and come to teach something.

phrases.english: to make him liable for his sister
who is his father's sister
who is his mother's sister.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא אָמַר קְרָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the refuted קל וחומר from steps 11-12 with a direct source from a פסוק.
steps.raayaObject: That a man is liable separately for each label of one woman (sister, father's sister, mother's sister).
steps.raayaSupportSource: The extra words 'עֶרְוַת אֲחוֹתוֹ גִלָּה' in ויקרא 20:17.

steps.title: How one woman can be sister, father's sister and mother's sister
steps.stepSummary: רב אדא בר אהבה describes a real family where this can happen: a wicked man, son of a wicked man.
steps.simpleTranslation: A man had relations with his mother and fathered two daughters. Then he had relations with one of those daughters and fathered a son. If that son has relations with the other daughter, she is his mother's sister, his own sister, and his father's sister. So the son is wicked, and so was his father.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אדא בר אהבה explains how the case in step 13 can actually happen. It sounds impossible, so he builds a real family tree.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The grandfather's two daughters are also his sisters, because they share a mother. The son is born from one daughter, so the other daughter is his mother's sister. She is also his sister, because they share a father, and she is his father's sister, because she is the sister of the first man, who is both the son's father and his grandfather.

keyTerms.meaning: You can find it; shows how a case can really happen
A wicked man, son of a wicked man
Fathered (a child)

steps.confusionAlert: Keep the three people straight: the first man (who is both the son's father and his grandfather), his two daughters, and the son. The woman with three labels is the daughter who is NOT the son's mother.

phrases.english: Rav Adda bar Ahava said:
You find it
in a wicked man, son of a wicked man,
who had relations with his mother
and fathered two daughters,
and then had relations with one of them
and fathered a son,
and his son had relations with his mother's sister,
who is his sister,
who is his father's sister,
so he is a wicked man, son of a wicked man.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב אַדָּא בַּר אַהֲבָה מַשְׁכַּחַתְּ לַהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shows that the case taught by the פסוק in step 13 can really happen.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The case happens when a man's son by his own daughter has relations with that man's other daughter, whom he fathered with his own mother.

steps.title: Repeated acts with the same woman: one חטאת or many?
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא brings a dispute. רבי אליעזר says each act with the same forbidden woman needs its own חטאת. The חכמים say only one.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Rabbis taught: if a man had relations with her, and again, and again, רבי אליעזר says he is liable for each time. The חכמים say he is liable for only one.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new topic with a ברייתא. Before, the question was many labels on one woman. Now it is many acts with the same woman.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question is whether repeated acts done in one lapse count as separate sins. רבי אליעזר counts each act on its own. The חכמים say one lapse of forgetting makes all the acts one sin, so there is one חטאת.

keyTerms.meaning: And again had relations with her; the act was repeated
Liable for each and every one
The Sages, the majority opinion
He is liable only once

phrases.english: The Rabbis taught:
If he had relations with her,
and again had relations with her,
and again had relations with her,
he is liable for each and every one,
these are the words of Rabbi Eliezer.
But the Sages say:
he is liable for only one.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן בָּא עָלֶיהָ וְחָזַר וּבָא עָלֶיהָ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from many labels on one woman to many acts with one woman.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי אליעזר: a separate חטאת for each act. חכמים: only one חטאת.

steps.title: The חכמים agree in the case of five wives
steps.stepSummary: The חכמים agree with רבי אליעזר that a man who is with his five wives who are נדות in one lapse brings a חטאת for each, since he caused each of them to need a חטאת.
steps.simpleTranslation: The חכמים agree with רבי אליעזר about a man who had relations with his five wives who were נדות in one lapse. He is liable for each one, since he caused each of them to need a חטאת.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא adds a case where even the חכמים agree that there are many חטאות.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here the question is not about repeating an act with one woman. There are five different women, and each one now needs her own חטאת because of him. Since he caused five separate sins, he brings five חטאות.

keyTerms.meaning: And the Sages agree
Women in their time of נדה, forbidden to their husbands
At one time; here, in one lapse of forgetting
Since he caused them (to need a חטאת)

steps.whatToRemember: Even the חכמים, who say one חטאת for repeated acts with one woman, agree that five wives means five חטאות. He caused each wife her own sin.
steps.whyThisMatters: This links back to the five-wives case from רבן גמליאל and רבי יהושע in step 10. It gives a reason why each wife counts on her own.

phrases.english: And the Sages agree with Rabbi Eliezer
about one who had relations with his five wives who were נדות
at one time,
phrases.notes: This means all in one lapse of forgetting, not literally at the same moment.

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁהוּא חַיָּיב עַל כׇּל אַחַת וְאַחַת,
phrases.english: that he is liable for each and every one,
since he caused them.
phrases.notes: Because of him, each wife now has to bring her own חטאת.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמוֹדִים חֲכָמִים לְרַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Limits the חכמים's view from step 15 by naming a case where they agree to many חטאות.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A man with five wives who are נדות, in one lapse, brings five חטאות, because he caused each wife to need a חטאת.

steps.title: רבא challenges the reason 'since he caused them'
steps.stepSummary: רבא asks רב נחמן: can the reason really be that he caused each wife to bring a חטאת? A ברייתא shows a man who caused a woman to bring five חטאות, yet he brings only one.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said to רב נחמן: Do we really say 'since he caused them'? But a ברייתא teaches: if he was in one lapse of awareness and she was in five lapses of awareness, he is liable for only one חטאת, and she is liable for each and every one.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא attacks the reason given in step 16 for why the man brings five חטאות for his five wives.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 16 said he brings five חטאות because he caused each wife to need one. רבא shows a case where a man caused a woman to bring five חטאות, yet he brings only one. So 'he caused them' cannot be the real reason.

keyTerms.meaning: Since, because
Caused
A lapse of awareness, a stretch of time when the person forgot it was forbidden
Liable, must bring a קרבן

phrases.english: Rava said to Rav Nachman:
Do we really say "since he caused them" to bring a חטאת?
But isn't it taught in a ברייתא:
He was in one lapse of awareness
phrases.notes: Some versions have the word in round brackets; the corrected wording is in square brackets. Both mean 'one'.

phrases.english: and she was in five lapses of awareness,
he is liable for only one חטאת,

phrases.aramaic: וְהִיא חַיֶּיבֶת עַל כׇּל אַחַת וְאֶחָת.
phrases.english: and she is liable for each and every one.

steps.triggerLanguage: מִי אָמְרִינַן ״הוֹאִיל וְהוּא גָּרַם לָהֶן״? וְהָתַנְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the reason given in step 16.
steps.kashyaTarget: The reason 'since he caused them' for five separate חטאות.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: In the ברייתא he caused her to bring five חטאות, yet he brings only one. So causing others to bring many does not make him bring many.

steps.title: The real reason: five separate bodies
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא changes the reason. He brings five חטאות because the five wives are five separate people.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, say: since they are separate bodies.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers רבא by swapping in a better reason for the חכמים's ruling about the five wives.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ruling stays the same, but the reason changes. It is not about causing them to bring חטאות. It is that each sin was with a different person. In the ברייתא there was only one woman, so he brings only one.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather, say this instead (fixing an earlier statement)
Separate bodies, different people

steps.whatToRemember: Five wives mean five חטאות because they are five different people, not because he caused them to bring חטאות.

phrases.english: Rather, say:
since they are separate bodies.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא אֵימָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רבא's challenge by restating the reason.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: He brings five because he caused each wife to bring a חטאת.
steps.terutzMaskana: He brings five because the five wives are separate bodies.

steps.title: What about reaping twice on שבת?
steps.stepSummary: A new question: if someone reaped, and reaped again, on שבת in one lapse of awareness, what would רבי אליעזר say?
steps.simpleTranslation: A question was asked: if he reaped and then reaped again, what would רבי אליעזר say?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new question. It asks whether רבי אליעזר's rule from step 15 (a separate חטאת for each act) also applies to reaping on שבת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אליעזר said each act with the same forbidden woman needs its own חטאת. Now the גמרא wants to know if he would say the same about two acts of reaping on שבת done in one lapse of awareness.

keyTerms.meaning: A question was raised before the חכמים
Reaped, one of the forbidden מלאכות on שבת

phrases.english: A question was asked of them:
if he reaped and then reaped again,
phrases.notes: He means on שבת, each time enough to need a חטאת, all in one lapse of awareness.

phrases.english: what would רבי אליעזר say?

steps.triggerLanguage: אִיבַּעְיָא לְהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new question based on רבי אליעזר's view from step 15.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Does רבי אליעזר require a separate חטאת for each act of reaping on שבת in one lapse of awareness?

steps.title: First side: he did two acts
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא lays out one side of the question. Maybe רבי אליעזר's reason is that he did two separate acts. If so, reaping twice is also two acts.
steps.simpleTranslation: Is the reason of רבי אליעזר there because he did two acts, and that is why he says he is liable for each and every one? Then here too, he did two acts.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is explaining why the question is a real question. It starts with the side that says he would bring two חטאות, and is setting up the other side.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If רבי אליעזר's reason is simply 'he did two acts,' then reaping twice is the same: two acts, two חטאות. The other side of the question will come next.

keyTerms.meaning: The reason
There, in the earlier case of forbidden relations
Here too
Two

phrases.english: Is the reason of רבי אליעזר there
phrases.notes: 'There' means the case from step 15: being with the same forbidden woman several times.

phrases.english: because he did two acts,
and because of this he says:
phrases.notes: Some versions have the extra letter in round brackets and some don't. The meaning is the same.

phrases.english: he is liable for each and every one?
Then here too, he did two acts,

steps.triggerLanguage: טַעְמָא דְּרַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר הָתָם מִשּׁוּם דְּהוּא דַּעֲבַד תַּרְתֵּין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Spells out the first side of the question from step 19.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Is רבי אליעזר's reason simply that he did two separate acts? If so, it would apply to reaping as well.

steps.title: The other side: maybe the reason is that the acts cannot be joined
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא gives the second possible reason for רבי אליעזר. In forbidden relations, the separate acts can never be joined into one, so each one needs its own חטאת. Reaping two fig-sized amounts can be joined into one act, so maybe only one חטאת is due. Which reason is right?
steps.simpleTranslation: Or maybe רבי אליעזר's reason there is that the acts of relations cannot be joined into one. That is why he says one is liable for each one. But if someone reaped a fig-sized amount, and then reaped another fig-sized amount in one lapse of awareness, he could have reaped both amounts at once. So he would owe only one חטאת. Which is it?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes laying out the question from Step 20. It gives the second possible reason for רבי אליעזר, which would lead to a different answer for reaping twice.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Reason 1 (Step 20) says each act counts on its own, so reaping twice means two חטאות. Reason 2 says the acts count separately only because they could never have been one act. Reaping can be done all at once, so under Reason 2 he owes just one חטאת.

keyTerms.meaning: Or perhaps: brings in the other side of a question
To combine them into one single act
The size of a dried fig, the minimum amount that makes one liable on שבת
One lapse of awareness, one period of forgetting

phrases.aramaic: אוֹ דִּלְמָא טַעְמֵיהּ דְּרַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר הָתָם
phrases.english: Or perhaps the reason of Rabbi Eliezer there
phrases.notes: "There" means the case from step 15: being with the same forbidden woman again and again.

phrases.english: is because it is impossible for him
to combine the acts of relations with one another,
and therefore Rabbi Eliezer said:
he is liable for each and every one,
but if he reaped a fig-sized amount
and then reaped another fig-sized amount
in one lapse of awareness,
phrases.notes: Both words mean "one." The word in square brackets is the corrected spelling.

phrases.english: since it is possible for him to combine
the two fig-sized amounts at the same time
he is liable for only one. What is the answer?

steps.triggerLanguage: אוֹ דִּלְמָא טַעְמֵיהּ דְּרַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר הָתָם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the two-sided question begun in Step 20 by giving the second possible reason.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Is רבי אליעזר's reason that there were two separate acts, or that the acts could not be combined? The answer decides the law for reaping twice.

steps.title: רבה: The reason is that he did two acts
steps.stepSummary: רבה answers that רבי אליעזר's reason is that the person did two separate acts. Reaping twice is also two acts, so he owes two חטאות.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה said: רבי אליעזר's reason there is that he did two acts. Here too, he did two acts.
steps.whatsHappening: רבה answers the question. He picks the first reason: two separate acts mean two חטאות, even for reaping.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבה, it does not matter whether the acts could have been joined. What counts is that two separate acts were actually done. So the man who reaped twice owes two חטאות, just like in the case of relations.

keyTerms.meaning: He did two separate acts
Here too: the same reasoning applies to this case

phrases.english: Rabba said:
The reason of Rabbi Eliezer there
is because he did two acts,
here too, he has done two acts.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבָּה: טַעְמָא דְּרַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר הָתָם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question by choosing the first side (Step 20).
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: According to רבי אליעזר, reaping twice in one lapse brings two חטאות because two acts were done.

steps.title: רב יוסף: The reason is that the acts cannot be joined
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף disagrees. He says רבי אליעזר's reason is that the acts of relations cannot be joined into one. When the acts can be joined, as with reaping, only one חטאת is due.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יוסף said: רבי אליעזר's reason there is that it is impossible to combine them. But where it is possible to combine them, he is liable for only one.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף gives the opposite answer. He picks the second reason from Step 21, so reaping twice brings only one חטאת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רב יוסף, the deciding question is whether the acts could have been one act. Acts of relations can never be one, so each counts. Two reapings could have been one, so they count as one.

keyTerms.meaning: Impossible
He is liable for only one חטאת

phrases.english: And Rav Yosef said:
The reason of Rabbi Eliezer there
is that it is impossible for him to combine them,
but where it is possible for him to combine them,
he is liable for only one.

steps.whatToRemember: רבה: two acts mean two חטאות, even for reaping. רב יוסף: separate חטאות only when the acts could never have been joined, so reaping twice means one חטאת.
steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַב יוֹסֵף אָמַר: טַעְמָא דְּרַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר הָתָם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives an opposing answer to רבה's, choosing the second side (Step 21).
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: According to רבי אליעזר, reaping twice in one lapse brings only one חטאת because the reapings could have been combined.

steps.title: אביי quotes a ברייתא about אבות and תולדות
steps.stepSummary: אביי begins a challenge against רבה. He quotes a ברייתא: רבי אליעזר makes a person liable for a תולדה even when he also did its אב in the same lapse.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי challenged רבה: רבי אליעזר makes one liable for subcategories of labor in a case where he also did the main categories of labor.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי quotes a source to set up an attack on רבה. The actual question comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא says that if someone does a main labor and also one of its sub-labors in one lapse, רבי אליעזר makes him bring two חטאות. אביי will draw an inference from this wording.

keyTerms.meaning: The main categories of labor forbidden on שבת
Sub-categories: labors that come from a main labor
Here: together with, in the same lapse as

phrases.english: Abaye raised an objection to Rabba:

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר מְחַיֵּיב עַל וַלְדֵי מְלָאכוֹת
phrases.english: Rabbi Eliezer makes one liable for subcategories of labor
together with main categories of labor.
phrases.notes: He means he did both the main labor and its sub-labor, so he brings a separate חטאת for each.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֵיתִיבֵיהּ אַבָּיֵי לְרַבָּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a challenge against רבה's answer from Step 22.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבה's explanation that רבי אליעזר's reason is that two acts were done.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Setup: a ברייתא that lists a main labor together with its sub-labor as the case of liability. The inference comes next.

steps.title: The same main labor twice is exempt, so how can רבה be right?
steps.stepSummary: From the ברייתא, אביי infers that doing the same main labor twice in one lapse brings only one חטאת. If רבי אליעזר's reason were "he did two acts," this person should owe two. Why is he exempt from a second one?
steps.simpleTranslation: This implies that if he did the same main labor and again the same main labor in one lapse, he is exempt from a second חטאת. But if you say רבי אליעזר's reason is that he did two acts, why is he exempt?
steps.whatsHappening: אביי makes his attack. He infers a rule from the ברייתא that seems to go against רבה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא names only the case of a main labor plus its sub-labor. That implies that the same main labor done twice brings only one חטאת. Doing the same labor twice is still two acts, so רבה's reason should require two חטאות. This fits רב יוסף better, since the same labor twice could have been done all at once.

keyTerms.meaning: The same main labor done twice
Here: in one lapse of awareness
Exempt, here from a second חטאת
Why?

steps.confusionAlert: אביי reads "בבת אחת" as "in one lapse of awareness," with the acts done one after the other. The answer in steps 26-27 reads it as truly at one moment, in one motion, and that is how רבה is saved.

phrases.aramaic: הָא אָב וְאָב, בְּבַת אַחַת – פָּטוּר.
phrases.english: This implies: a main labor and the same main labor, in one lapse, he is exempt.
phrases.notes: He is exempt from a second חטאת, not from bringing any חטאת at all.

phrases.english: And if you say the reason of Rabbi Eliezer
is because he did two acts,
why is he exempt?

steps.triggerLanguage: הָא אָב וְאָב, בְּבַת אַחַת פָּטוּר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws the inference from the ברייתא quoted in Step 24 and turns it against רבה.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבה's claim that for רבי אליעזר, two separate acts always bring two חטאות.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא implies that the same main labor done twice in one lapse brings only one חטאת, even though two acts were done. That goes against רבה's reason.

steps.title: The vine and the fig were cut at the same moment
steps.stepSummary: מר בריה דרבנן explains that the ברייתא is about a vine trained over a fig tree, where both were cut together. He is liable for two חטאות because the names of the labors and the objects are different.
steps.simpleTranslation: מר, son of the Sages, said: I and רב נחומי בר זכריה explained it this way. The ברייתא is about a climbing vine that hangs over a fig tree, and he cut both at the same time. רבי אליעזר makes him liable for two because there are two different labor names and two different objects.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers אביי's challenge against רבה. It shows that the ברייתא is about two things done at the exact same moment.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אביי had inferred that doing the same main labor twice brings only one חטאת. מר בריה דרבנן replies that the ברייתא is about one single motion that cut both the fig (an אב) and the vine (a תולדה). That one motion gets two חטאות only because the names and the objects are different. So the inference only teaches about acts done all at once.

keyTerms.meaning: "What case are we dealing with here?" The גמרא uses this to narrow a source to a specific situation.
A climbing grapevine that is trained to grow up over something
At the same time, in one motion
Separate names, meaning two different categories of labor (an אב and a תולדה)
Separate bodies, meaning two different physical objects

steps.confusionAlert: The key detail is "at the same time" (בבת אחת). The ברייתא is not about two acts done one after another. It is about one cut that covered two different things.

phrases.english: Mar, son of the Sages, said:

phrases.aramaic: אֲנָא וְרַב נְחוּמִי בַּר זְכַרְיָה תַּרְגֵּימְנָא:
phrases.english: I and Rav Nachumi bar Zecharya explained it:
phrases.notes: "It" is the ברייתא that אביי quoted against רבה.

phrases.english: What case are we dealing with here?
With a climbing vine trained over a fig tree
and he cut them both at once.
For that reason Rabbi Eliezer holds him liable,
since the names are separate
and the bodies are separate.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר מָר בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַבָּנַן: אֲנָא וְרַב נְחוּמִי בַּר זְכַרְיָה תַּרְגֵּימְנָא: הָכָא בְמַאי עָסְקִינַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers אביי's challenge to רבה by placing the ברייתא in a specific case
steps.terutzResolutionType: Narrowing the case (אוקימתא): the ברייתא is about one simultaneous cut
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא seemed to show that the same labor done twice, even one after the other, brings only one חטאת
steps.terutzMaskana: The ברייתא is about one cut of two things at once. Two חטאות are due there only because the names and objects are different.

steps.title: Reaping twice is exempt only when done at once
steps.stepSummary: The same logic applies to reaping. A person is exempt from a second חטאת only if he reaped two fig-sized amounts in one motion. If he reaped one and then another, he owes two, just as רבה said.
steps.simpleTranslation: In the matching case of reaping and reaping again, when would he be exempt? Only when he reaped two fig-sized amounts at the same time. But if he reaped a fig-sized amount and then went back and reaped another, he is liable.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes the answer. It shows that the inference from the ברייתא only covers reaping done all at once, so רבה's view stands.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The "exempt" case inferred from the ברייתא matches it exactly: one simultaneous act. Two separate acts of reaping, one after the other, still count as two acts. That is exactly רבה's reason for רבי אליעזר, so אביי's challenge falls away.

keyTerms.meaning: The matching or parallel case
A dried fig. It is the minimum amount for liability for carrying and for reaping on שבת.
To be exempt (here, from a second חטאת)

steps.whatToRemember: According to רבה, רבי אליעזר's rule is that separate acts mean separate חטאות. The ברייתא's "one חטאת" case is only when both amounts were reaped in one motion.

phrases.english: In the parallel case, where he reaped and reaped again,
how do you find that he is exempt?
phrases.notes: He means exempt from a second חטאת.

phrases.aramaic: כְּגוֹן שֶׁקָּצַר שְׁתֵּי גְּרוֹגְרוֹת בְּבַת אַחַת,
phrases.english: For example, where he reaped two fig-sized amounts at once.
But if he reaped a fig-sized amount
and then went back and reaped another fig-sized amount,
he is liable.
phrases.notes: Liable to bring two חטאות, one for each act.

steps.triggerLanguage: דִּכְווֹתַהּ קָצַר וְקָצַר, הֵיכִי מַשְׁכַּחַתְּ לַהּ דְּמִיפְּטַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies the narrowed case from Step 26 to the inference אביי drew in Step 25
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the inference to a simultaneous act
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Reaping twice would bring only one חטאת according to רבי אליעזר, which goes against רבה
steps.terutzMaskana: Only reaping two amounts at once brings one חטאת. Reaping twice, one after the other, brings two, which supports רבה.

steps.title: רבי עקיבא asks about a limb hanging loose from an animal
steps.stepSummary: A new משנה opens. רבי עקיבא asks what the law is for a limb that is still attached to an animal but hanging loose.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: And רבי עקיבא also asked: what is the law of a limb that is hanging loose on an animal?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to a new משנה. It continues the list of questions רבי עקיבא asked, and this time the topic is טומאה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A limb cut off a living animal makes things impure. The question is about a limb that is partly torn but still attached. Does it already count as a separate limb for טומאה?

keyTerms.meaning: Our משנה. It marks the start of a new משנה.
A dangling limb, still partly attached to the body
An animal

phrases.english: MISHNAH: And furthermore Rabbi Akiva asked:
A dangling limb on an animal, what is its law?
phrases.notes: He is asking whether it makes things impure like a limb that was fully cut off.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְנִי׳ וְעוֹד שָׁאַל רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה on a new topic
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The משנה opens with רבי עקיבא's question about the טומאה of a dangling limb on an animal

steps.title: רבן גמליאל and רבי יהושע answer from what they heard about a person
steps.stepSummary: רבן גמליאל and רבי יהושע say they have no tradition about an animal. They did hear that a dangling limb on a person is pure, and they begin to describe how people acted on that ruling.
steps.simpleTranslation: They said to him: We have not heard about that. But we have heard that a dangling limb on a person is pure, and so they would...
steps.whatsHappening: רבן גמליאל and רבי יהושע answer רבי עקיבא's question. They have no direct tradition, so they bring a related ruling about a person. The sentence continues on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: They admit they have no ruling about an animal. They do know that a limb still attached to a person does not carry the טומאה of a separate limb. The words "and so they would" set up a description of what people actually did, which continues on the next amud.

keyTerms.meaning: "We have not heard," meaning there is no tradition from our teachers on this
Ritually pure, does not cause טומאה

phrases.english: They said to him: We have not heard,
but we have heard about a dangling limb on a person
that it is pure,
and so they would...

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמְרוּ לוֹ: לֹא שָׁמַעְנוּ, אֲבָל שָׁמַעְנוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רבי עקיבא's question from Step 28
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The טומאה status of a dangling limb on an animal
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: There is no tradition about an animal. A dangling limb on a person is pure.
